summary: Contestants demonstrate skills needed in a professional legal office, including using legal terminology, creating and managing documents, maintaining compliance with data protection and ethical standards, and organizing office systems. The event includes tasks such as client service, legal research, and understanding court procedures. All work is completed on-site using provided computers and software.
time_limits: no more than ten (10) minutes orientation
no more than sixty (60) minutes testing time
no more than ten (10) minutes wrap-up
submission_requirements: All student-produced jobs completed on-site are uploaded electronically and are not printed at the national level
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Suggested resource: ANSI/ARMA 1-1995 - Alphabetic Filing Rules
competencies: Apply foundational legal terminology, including Latin terms, and office procedures to ensure accurate communication and compliance in a legal environment
Create, edit, and format legal documents and client correspondence using digital tools and industry-standard practices to ensure accuracy, clarity, and compliance
Manage electronic communications and files in compliance with legal protocols and data protection regulations
Deliver professional client service while upholding ethical standards and confidentiality requirements in all legal office interactions
Organize and maintain office inventory and filing systems using digital tools and ARMA standards
Research legal information and manage client records and billing procedures
Apply knowledge of federal, state, and local court structures and proceedings
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this application event.
